newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bank Indonesia says no plan to cancel swaps.
newsitem.headline: Bank Indonesia says no plan to cancel swaps.

text.p: Bank Indonesia said on Friday it has no current plans to follow steps taken by the Bank of Thailand asking Thai banks to stop quoting tomorrow/next swaps to offshore investors.
"We have no intention to freeze the swap facility for now," Bambang Trianto, director of the central bank's foreign exchange department, told Reuters.
"But we are watching the market very closely."

Trianto was speaking in response to speculation that Bank Indonesia could implement such steps. Indonesia's currency market was jolted in the morning on talk that the Malaysian monetary authority had also asked its local banks to stop quoting tomorrow/next swaps to offshore parties.
However, Malaysia's central bank, Bank Negara, denied on Friday that it had told banks to stop undertaking swap transations.
"We are comfortable with market rates," Trianto said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,434/36 to the dollar at 0350 GMT after soaring to a high of 2,413 from an opening of 2,444.0/45.0.
Trianto said offshore investors seemed to be hedging their positions, especially with one-month swaps, a move which was linked to the general election on May 29.
